# Boundary reduction strategy

## Question

We need your mathematical critique and a concrete general algorithm for reducing boundary data in a reverse-unitarity NNLO double-real DE computation. User wants genuinely few simpler boundary integrals, not thousands of generic-point constants. General framework, no family-specific hardcoding, no backward compatibility constraint.

Current verified data: 91 families, 345 nonzero coefficient-requested master integrals (347 final coefficient entries, two exactly zero), 1561 family-labelled master positions in closed derivative systems. Saved explicit finite epsilon solutions I(X,eps)=U(X,X0,eps) C(eps) (actual finite expressions, no lazy generator). These reference 1556 original-basis ordinary-point master series and 8811 Laurent coefficients; 90 families X0=(1/4,1/6), CF269 X0=(1/4,1/3). Family-local labels have not been reconciled. Full strict epsilon form unnecessary; algebraic homogeneous blocks and triangular epsilon-zero preparation already solved all91. Original global Kira stream retains347 masters,352 declared masters,374 families, exact IBP rules. We will try to express derivative-closure lower sectors in this global basis through existing rules and exact cut-preserving topology maps.

Historical claims: an earlier nullity census said <=33 boundary period types. Partial39-family physical campaign had20 structural period IDs, three known-zero IDs,17 remaining types represented by42 conservative family-local series and79 demanded eps coefficients. Not current91 coverage. Later correction: CF300 zero residue eigenspace genuinely2D; grouping by one period ID incorrectly merged two directions absent a tangential DE+endpoint relation. Old nullity design imposed R_normal F=0 on boundary, branch absence, volume anchors, regularity, claiming dedup by block/mode/class. Need critically assess what is legitimate. Many old generated results were deleted; source code and design records retained.

Please think through:
1. What is the most effective sequence from these current finite ordinary-point solutions to a small set of simpler physical boundary integrals? Exact global IBP/topology quotient first? Singular matching per maximal sector, with inherited lower sectors? Alternative particularly effective for cut phase-space integrals?
2. Distinguish generic DE rank, number of independent boundary series over Q(eps), structural period types, epsilon-coefficient slots, and actual new integrals to evaluate. Why 345 requested integrals doesn't directly bound naive family closures, and when a <=345 global bound is justified.
3. Give mathematically correct implementable constraint equations at singular strata for noncanonical systems: integer valuations, z^(a+b eps), logs, source terms, normal+tangential compatibility, regularized connection to X0. Specifically when R F=0 is valid and when it incorrectly removes physical modes.
4. We can use rational/modular/numerical checks cheaply (eventual AMFlow). How can we obtain a reliable upper bound quickly without computing costly full analytic connection matrices? Can local regularity at spurious poles / cut-domain symmetries provide constraints directly on global ordinary-point constants? What exact evidence must be retained?
5. Propose minimal general data model and implementation milestone that actually reduces current unknowns. Avoid claiming a dozen count from eigenvalues/type labels alone. Challenge our plan if it cannot recover the promised reduction.

Please be concrete with equations, algorithms and caution about degeneracies. We will implement while you think. No need for literature citations unless a specific primary reference helps.

## Pro response

Your global IBP/topology quotient is the correct first step. The historical “≤33 period types” is not a defensible bound on the current 91-family problem, and residue-nullity counting alone cannot recover such a bound. The CF300 correction exposes the central issue: a shared exponent or period label does not identify independent solution directions.

I would organize the calculation around two distinct reductions:

family-labelled ordinary-point data⟶global DE data⟶explicit simpler physical boundary integrals.

1. What the different counts mean

These quantities should have separate fields in the implementation.

Quantity	Mathematical meaning
Generic DE rank r	Dimension over Q(X,ϵ), or the declared algebraic extension, of the derivative-closed module generated by the requested integrals.
Rationally independent boundary series	Dimension of the span of specified boundary integrals over Q(ϵ), after established boundary IBP and other rational relations.
Remaining DE input amplitudes d	Number of free series after imposing the currently established physical constraints. The coefficient field of those constraints must be specified.
Structural period types	A classification of integrands, regions, geometries, or exponent patterns. Not a linear-algebraic dimension.
Laurent-coefficient slots	Scalar coefficients needed after propagating valuations and target-order demands. Relations can couple different orders.
New integrals to evaluate p	Concrete unevaluated simpler integrals in a constructive boundary representation, after reusing known anchors and established relations.

For your present data:

A complete exact reduction of the closed systems into the 347 retained global masters would establish a spanning bound of 347 for the target differential module.

A bound of 345 requires an additional certificate: the requested integrals span a derivative-closed space of dimension at most 345, or the relevant global space admits sufficient further exact relations.

The 352 declared masters are a declaration count, not a demonstrated rank.

Moreover, symmetry deduplication alone is insufficient: different family master choices can remain IBP-linearly dependent even after pairwise symmetry duplicates are removed. This is explicitly encountered in large cut-integral calculations.

The old 39-family campaign remains useful as a collection of candidate definitions and relations, but neither its 17 remaining types nor its 42 local series can be extrapolated to current coverage. In particular, CF300’s two directions remain two until an actual relation or sufficient boundary conditions remove one.

There are two important qualifications.

First, your variables must genuinely admit this measurement interpretation. Integrating an arbitrary external invariant does not automatically remove a cut propagator. An additional external phase-space integration and its Jacobian may be necessary, or the resulting problem may be harder rather than simpler.

Second, endpoint integration must respect dimensional regularization. Choose weights that make coefficientwise integration legitimate, or retain the dimensional powers and perform endpoint subtraction/analytic continuation before expanding. Weighted matching designed to compensate endpoint powers is used precisely for this reason. 
arxiv.org

For distributions, weights that vanish at an endpoint can miss endpoint-supported terms. Those terms must either already be fixed by the regulated integral definition or be included in the matching.

A useful positive example exists: a double-real soft system has been determined from an inclusive phase-space volume alone. But that calculation also explicitly observes that more complicated systems need additional boundary information. It supports testing this route, not assuming a universal one-volume answer. 
arXiv

The reason is simple: continuation of a complete local germ determines a solution, so restriction to that germ is injective. For each block, any one valid stratum bound bounds its remaining homogeneous freedom. Bottom-up addition then gives the displayed bound.

This requires neither a full connection matrix nor intersections between differently based local subspaces.

Do not add codimensions from different strata without transporting the constraints into a common space. They may express the same condition. Taking the minimum of the separate bounds is conservative; summing their apparent reductions is not.

The word complete matters: retain vanishing integer-power modes, logarithmic chains, and later resonant free coefficients. An incomplete region classification should enlarge the admissible space, not shrink it.

Equation (9) bounds remaining DE inputs. To obtain an upper bound on new simpler integral evaluations, also exhibit a finite set of explicitly defined boundary integrals spanning the required germs. That is a stronger, constructive statement.

Spurious singularities need a physical analyticity statement

Regularity at a spurious pole can constrain physical solutions, but not merely because the DE matrix has a pole there.

If the singularity is apparent and every solution is regular in the physical integral basis, regularity imposes no new condition. Conversely, a singular gauge can make perfectly regular integrals look singular.

5. Minimal data model and an implementation milestone

I would retain five mathematical record types.

Record	Essential content
Integral definition	Denominators and powers, numerator, cut orientations, prescriptions, measure normalization, regulators, and physical domain. Family labels are aliases.
Global reduction	Global representatives, sparse exact maps from all closure positions, target demands, reference points, and necessary basepoint bridges.
Boundary chart	Coordinate map, accessible domain component, local gauge, full mode/jet basis, tangential DE, and established admissibility conditions.
Boundary integral	Explicit limiting or inclusive integral definition, normalization, boundary IBP reduction, and known evaluation where available. Structural type is metadata only.
Relation	Sparse equations, their coefficient field and Laurent range, and the mathematical evidence: exact map, recurrence plus physical condition, moment identity, or certified rank witness.

No large provenance apparatus is needed. But every removed direction must be traceable to an actual equation and its assumptions. A period label, numerical resemblance, or old census entry is not sufficient evidence.

First milestone: remove ordinary-point duplication in the existing outputs

Produce and apply the sparse substitutions for all mapped common-point constants. Report unresolved closure positions separately, and handle the CF269 bridge only where needed.

This milestone should change the saved explicit finite expressions and their demand graph. It should report the global spanning bound and remaining independent input representation—not merely a new list of canonical labels.

Completion criterion

The campaign has delivered the requested reduction only when it can report:

	​

coverage of all requested outputs,
number of unresolved ordinary-point input series,
number and definitions of new simpler boundary integrals,
their demanded Laurent coefficients,
explicit substitutions into the existing finite solutions.
	​


The unresolved ordinary-point count should be zero for a claimed complete boundary reduction. A small residual-mode bound is useful before that point, but it is not the same deliverable.

My principal challenge to the plan is this: global quotienting can plausibly turn the present bookkeeping problem into a few hundred global inputs, but it cannot by itself turn those into a few physical integrals. That second reduction must come from the IBP structure of actual limiting or inclusive cut integrals, plus correctly matched physical conditions. If many amplitudes remain, change the degeneration or add rank-increasing moment relations; do not make the residue-kernel rule more aggressive.
